'You don't know that.'

Team notes, Monday 14th
Nilesh told me before stand-up that the hospital client 'will obviously reject' our revised scheduling proposal, because they complained about the demo. He'd already started drafting a fallback. I noticed a small pull in myself to promise him they'd love it, which would have been my own guess dressed up as fact. Instead I asked him to treat his prediction as a guess and test it: write down what he expects them to say and how sure he is, then send the proposal as planned. He wrote: 'Reject. 85% sure. They'll say too complex.'
Friday 18th
The client replied. They accepted two of the three modules, rejected the third as too complex, and asked for a call. Nilesh laughed and said he was one-third right. I was two-thirds right, which surprised me too. Next step: share his note with the team as an example of testing a forecast.
Pooja

This morning, packing the laptop for the pitch to the bakery chain, Lakshmi said, 'Honestly, why bother? They'll say no. They've used the same agency for years.' Akash got his physics unit test back this morning: 9 out of 30. He put the paper face down and didn't open his lunchbox. At the end of the day I found him still at his desk.
